title: Tenant-delimited privilege model and admin safeguards for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Overview: Define and prototype a tenant-delimited RBAC v2 role model that enforces least-privilege across nested resources (organization -> project -> dataset -> model) while providing safe admin controls and audit hooks. This ticket covers the role/permission model, SSO/SAML claim-to-role mapping, audit log events for sensitive actions, and emergency admin safeguards (breakglass, time-limited elevation, separation-of-duties warnings). Goals: 1) Produce a permission matrix for primary resources and operations that supports inheritance and explicit deny. 2) Design mapping rules from external identity providers (SAML attributes / SCIM groups) to internal role assignments without granting cross-tenant admin privileges. 3) Specify audit event schema and retention requirements for regulator-ready logs. 4) Define operational guardrails for breakglass, request throttling, and approval workflows for elevated actions. Constraints: Must be backwards-compatible with existing RBAC v1 assignments during migration window; minimal latency impact for token validation and permission checks; support multi-tenant isolation and cross-tenant limited shared roles (read-only reporting).
acceptance_criteria: Permission matrix documented for organization, project, dataset, model resources and exported as CSV in Confluence.
Canonical claim-to-role mapping documented with examples for Okta and Azure AD (SAML/SCIM).
Audit event schema (JSON) defined and approved by Compliance; sample events ingested into staging Grafana/Kibana dashboards.
Implementation plan for DB migration and enforcement middleware with feature-flag rollout exists.
Breakglass flow implemented behind feature flag: time-limited token issuance, escalation email, and audit event generation.
Security review completed and signoff from security@redwood-inference.com.
implementation_notes: DB: Add 'role_assignments' table with columns: id, principal_type, principal_id, tenant_id, resource_path, role_id, explicit_deny (boolean), created_at, expires_at. Migration script in GH: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7592.
Middleware: New fast-path permission check for reads (cacheable) and slower authz path for write/privileged ops with explicit deny evaluation.

SSO: Implement attribute mapping service that ingests SAML groups or SCIM groups and emits normalized role assignments. Draft mapping config: https://docs.redwood.com/ops/rbac-v2/sso-mapping (internal Drive).

Audit: Emit audit events for role changes, breakglass issuance, sensitive API calls (model delete, export keys). Event schema v1: {"timestamp","actor","action","resource_path","prev_roles","new_roles","reason","request_id","auth_method"}. Store to s3://redwood-audit/staging and forward to SIEM.
Console: Add role/assignment UI for tenant admins with 'preview effective permissions' that shows inherited vs explicit binds and any denies.
Migration: Phase 1 - read-only compatibility mode; Phase 2 - gradual enforcement for non-admin ops; Phase 3 - enforcement for admin-level ops with canary tenants.
audit_requirements: All role assignment changes must write an immutable audit event with actor and justification.
Breakglass issuance must include expiration and require a recorded justification; auto-revoke on expiry with audit event.
Retention: 7 years for role-change events for enterprise customers (configurable per-tenant); default retention 90 days.
Event forwards: Send high-severity events to PagerDuty channel and SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) with structured fields for searchability.
ssO_mapping_examples: Okta SAML example: Attribute: roles -> values: [Redwood:org_admin] -> map to internal role 'org:admin' limited to Okta tenant_id claim.
Azure AD SCIM example: group 'redwood.project.power-users' -> map to internal role 'project:editor' for specific tenant_id from SAML claim.
Explicit deny pattern: SCIM group 'suspended' maps to an assignment with explicit_deny=true for all write operations.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Mis-mapped SSO claims could grant cross-tenant admin rights. Mitigation: Mapping service enforces tenant_id in all role mappings and denies mappings missing tenant context.
Risk: Audit log loss during incident. Mitigation: Dual-write to S3 and pubsub queue; fallback local buffer with backfill job.
Risk: Performance regression on hot permission checks. Mitigation: LRU cache with TTL, separate caches for read vs write paths, and circuit-breaker for SIEM forwarding.
Risk: Human error in breakglass usage. Mitigation: Breakglass requires justification, email confirmation to security@, and auto-expiry; enforce MFA for issuance.
